rationale: Email deliverability engineers running PowerMTA face revenue-blocking TSS04/TSS05 deferrals from Yahoo/AOL with no vendor-supplied diagnostic tooling; the pain recurs across multiple public forums and affects companies whose livelihood depends on inbox placement. Existing paid tools (MXToolbox, GlockApps) explicitly do not cover PowerMTA deferral-code pattern analysis, and PowerMTA's own license cost (~$10k+/year) confirms a paying, professional buyer segment. At least one clear willingness-to-pay signal exists: competitors charge for deliverability monitoring subscriptions in the $99–$499/month range, and job postings for 'email deliverability engineer' roles are frequent.
